children: With a flurry of IPOs that Dalal Street has seen since June, a number of companies will now start to see their respective shareholder lock-ins end across various time periods. As many as 15 companies will see equity supply worth over ₹16,000 crore come into the market during the course of the week, with lock-ins of 10 companies scheduled to end as early as today. Here's a look at the complete list for the week.
Deepa Jewellers, Rays of Belief, Purple Style Labs, Priority Jewels, ESDS Software, Knack Packaging, SAi Parenteral's, Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar, TruAlt Bio Energy and EPack Prefab
are companies whose lock-in ends on Monday. Apart from these 10, Coal India's subsidiary
CMPDI, Pace Digitek, Glottis, Valiant Labs and Om Freight Forwarders
are the other five companies whose lock-in will end during the course of the week.

It must be noted that the end of the shareholder lock-in period does not mean that all the shares will be sold in the open market. They only become eligible to be traded. Lock-ins for two companies each ends on Tuesday and Wednesday, while one will see its lock-in end on Friday.

children: Among the companies whose lock-in ends this week, Coal India's subsidiary
Central Mine Planning and Design Institute (CMPDI)

has the biggest share in terms of value. The company's six-month shareholder lock-in will end on Tuesday, October 6, making 464 million shares of the company, or 65% of its outstanding equity eligible to be traded, according to Nuvama Alternative and Quantitative Research's Abhilash Pagaria's note. Based on Thursday's closing price, the total value of shares that will become eligible to be traded is worth ₹9,512 crore. Shares of CMPDI are down 28% from their post-listing high of over ₹280, but are still 20% above their issue price of ₹179.
